summary.name: Q, ChatGPT for Slack
summary.one_liner: Q is a Slack app powered by OpenAI's GPT that lets teams chat with ChatGPT-style AI inside their Slack workspace by mentioning @Q.
use_cases: Summarizing or evaluating URLs and files shared in Slack
Drafting emails, translations, and blog or social posts with team rules
Brainstorming and Q&A inside a Slack channel
Reviewing or testing code based on internal info
Sharing a single GPT chat with a whole team
summary.what_it_does: Q is a Slack app that brings ChatGPT-style conversation into a Slack workspace; users invite Q to a channel or DM and mention @Q to chat. It can read supported URLs (such as arXiv papers, YouTube, Google Docs/Sheets/Slides, and Notion) and many file types (audio, video, images, Excel, PowerPoint, Word, text, CSV, code) when attached to a message. Some URLs can be read with authentication, such as Google Workspace apps. Teams can set Custom Instructions with shared rules and templates that apply across the workspace. The page says Q reads only the thread it is mentioned in and does not store or use conversation content for training.
notable: Reads supported URLs and attached files on demand, including authenticated Google Workspace links
Team-wide Custom Instructions for shared rules and templates
Reads only the Slack thread where it is mentioned; states it does not save or train on conversations
Officially approved Slack app powered by OpenAI, per the page description
caveats: Free trial lasts 14 days; continued use requires a paid plan, with workspace as the billing unit
Output may be inaccurate or offensive, per the page's disclaimer
OpenAI retains conversation content for up to 30 days for abuse monitoring
